title: Rapid strep test (strep throat)
what: A swab is taken from your throat. In a few minutes, the test shows if strep is there. Strep is a germ that often causes strep throat.
why: For a sore throat with fever and white spots on the tonsils, to find out if you need an antibiotic.
duration: the swab takes a few seconds; results usually come in 5 to 15 minutes
tell_doctor: If you already started an antibiotic
If you recently gargled with an antiseptic

prepare.title: Food and drink
prepare.text: Usually do not eat or drink for 1 to 2 hours before the swab. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Throat
prepare.text: In the morning, do not gargle or use throat sprays or lozenges.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you already took. They will decide.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: You sit and open your mouth wide
Your tongue is held down with a flat stick
A swab is quickly rubbed over the tonsils and the back of the throat
The swab is dipped in liquid and the test is started
In a few minutes, the result shows on a strip
feel: You may gag for a second
after: The result is usually given right away
If the test is positive, your doctor will decide if you need an antibiotic
If the test is negative but you have signs of strep throat, a throat culture is sometimes done too

faq.q: If the test is negative, does that mean no strep throat?
faq.a: Not always. Sore throats are often caused by viruses. If there is still doubt, the doctor may order a throat culture.

faq.q: Why test if strep throat is obvious?
faq.a: It is hard to tell strep from a virus just by looking. The test helps you avoid antibiotics you do not need.

reminders.text: Throat swab soon. For 1 to 2 hours before, do not eat, drink, or gargle, unless the clinic said otherwise.
